pr.title: Make the enum check work for negative discriminants
pr.description:
The discriminant check was not working correctly for negative numbers. This change fixes that by masking out the relevant bits correctly.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#143218.
pr.author: 1c3t3a

issues.title: New enum discrimintant check doesn't work for negative numbers
issues.body: I tried this code: ```rust #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] enum Foo { Negative = -1, Positive = 1, } #[test] fn t() { let transmuted: Foo = unsafe { std::mem::transmute::(-1) }; assert_eq!(transmuted, Foo::Negative); } ``` I expected to see this happen: The test passes Instead, this happened: ``` thread 't' panicked at src/lib.rs:10:9: trying to construct an enum from an invalid value 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting. ``` ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.90.0-nightly (11ad40bb8 2025-06-28) binary: rustc commit-hash: 11ad40bb839ca16f74784b4ab72596ad85587298 commit-date: 2025-06-28 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.90.0-nightly LLVM version: 20.1.7 ``` Playground link: https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=c5012dd5ec0afc1bea52e85e81ff28e9 Seems to be related to https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/141759

analysis.originalLogic: `insert_direct_enum_check` first retained the discriminant through `insert_discr_cast_to_u128`, then used `Operand::Copy(discr)` directly as the `SwitchInt` discriminant. Switch targets were built with `discriminants.into_iter().map(|discr| (discr, new_block))`, and the invalid-construction assert also reported `Operand::Copy(discr)`. Thus the generated check compared a u128 cast of the discriminant, without reducing it to the enum's discriminant width.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation omitted width normalization: it forwarded the sign-extended u128 value from the discriminant cast directly to `SwitchInt`, left target constants untruncated, and used that same unmasked value in `AssertKind::InvalidEnumConstruction`. For a negative source such as `-1` stored in a narrow enum, sign extension yields an all-ones u128 rather than the narrow bit pattern expected by the target constants. The fix adds `let mask = discr.size.unsigned_int_max();`, masks with `BinOp::BitAnd`, truncates each target via `discr.size.truncate(discr_val)`, and reports `discr_masked`.
analysis.inputDomain: Direct enum-construction checks during MIR transformation, compiled with debug assertions, for enums having explicit negative discriminants (including narrow representations and `#[repr(i64)]`), where an unsafe transmute supplies a bit pattern for the enum's discriminant type. The transformed check must accept every valid discriminant, including negative and integer-boundary values, and reject invalid bit patterns.
analysis.summary: CheckEnums' direct discriminant check must normalize a cast discriminant to the enum's discriminant width before `SwitchInt` and invalid-value reporting. Without masking/truncation, negative discriminants are sign-extended to u128 and valid negative enum values are rejected.
analysis.trigger: An enum with an explicit negative discriminant, such as `A = -2`, `B = -1`, is checked for invalid construction after an unsafe transmute; the generated switch uses a sign-extended u128 instead of the enum-sized bits.
preconditions: The direct enum check in `check_enums.rs` is active, exercised here with `-C debug-assertions`.
The enum has explicit discriminants that include negative values.
An unsafe construct such as `std::mem::transmute` produces or attempts to produce the enum value, invoking the generated enum-construction check.
pitfalls: Signed-to-u128 casting sign-extends negative discriminants; comparing the result directly against narrow discriminant constants is incorrect.
Masking must use the discriminant size (`discr.size.unsigned_int_max()`), not an assumed 128-bit width.
Switch target constants must also be truncated with `discr.size.truncate(discr_val)`; masking only the scrutinee is insufficient if constants retain a different width/representation.
The diagnostic assertion must report the normalized `discr_masked` value; otherwise the check's reported invalid value is wrong even if branching is corrected.
Do not infer that positive-discriminant tests cover this bug: the issue's failure specifically produced `0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` for a negative value.
analysis.testStrategy: Build paired Rust UI tests with debug assertions. Positive case: enums with negative and positive discriminants, including narrow values and `#[repr(i64)]` variants at `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX`; transmute each valid underlying integer into the enum and assert equality with the expected variant. Negative case: an enum with `A = -2, B = -1, C = 1`; transmute an invalid `i8` such as `-3` and use a `run-fail` test with `error-pattern: trying to construct an enum from an invalid value 0xfd`, confirming the value is masked to the i8 bit pattern. No compiler execution was performed while extracting this knowledge.
